reason: The paper rider can show whether a point on the cord travels along with the wiggle.
expectation: The rider will move with its part of the cord, making the motion easier to observe.

effect: The rider showed that the disturbance travels along the cord while the rider stays near its own place. Next I’ll prepare the cord to play as a string.
reaction: The distinction between the travelling wave and the bobbing rider was satisfying to see.
reason: The movable bridge should give the cord a defined vibrating length for playing.

choice.with: Wave cord with a paper rider

expectation: The bridge will support the cord and prepare it to be plucked.

effect: The bridge has no available combination yet, so I need to find what prepares the cord for it.
reaction: I was surprised the bridge could not be fitted yet.
reason: Inspecting the wave cord should reveal which action is currently available.

choice.inspect: Wave cord with a paper rider

expectation: The compatibility list will show how to continue toward playing the cord.

choice.with: Wave cord with a paper rider

alternatives.reason: Adjusting the tension might be the required next step, but I am not sure.

effect: Adjusting tension and speed produced a standing pattern with two loops and a nearly still point. I’ll try preparing the cord for playing next.
reaction: The nearly still point between moving loops is intriguing.
reason: The bridge may now be ready to give the cord a defined vibrating length.
expectation: The bridge will support the cord for plucking.

alternatives.reason: I could check the available next action, but the bridge seems worth trying.

effect: The bridge now defines a movable vibrating length and transfers vibration to the soundbox. The cord appears ready to pluck.
reaction: The soundbox and soft feet give the bridge a more interesting role than I expected.
reason: The plectrum is the remaining tool for playing the cord like a string.

choice.with: Cord resting on a movable bridge

expectation: Plucking the cord will make it vibrate and produce a sound.

effect: Plucking completed the machine and showed that shortening the vibrating length raises the note; the earlier wave pattern can also be restored.
reaction: Comparing the two notes made the bridge’s purpose clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Plucking with the movable bridge was worthwhile because it connected a visible change in vibrating length to an audible change in pitch.

leastWorthwhile.text: The failed bridge attempt was the least worthwhile: the bridge seemed appropriate, but there was no visible indication that another observation had to come first.

surprise.text: The rider stayed near its own place while the disturbance travelled along the cord; the nearly still point between two moving loops was intriguing too.

arbitrary.text: The required order for fitting the bridge initially felt arbitrary, although the standing-wave observation it led to was useful.

continue.text: Yes, I would choose to continue: the rider, standing loops and changing pitch made the mechanisms worth exploring, despite the unclear ordering constraint.
